S-10-4 Kakizawa reviewed 14 inpatients with neurologic disease, including one Parkinson patient. Eleven retained oral intake through postdischarge home guidance. Diagnosis-specific results and foods are absent. A 2021 follow-up at the same site expands the cohort to 16, with one Parkinson patient again.

S-10-5 discusses timing medication before meals and medication-assistance jelly for conditions including Parkinson disease and myasthenia. No named ingredient, Parkinson treatment group or comparative outcome.

S-10-9 Tazumi reviewed 17 pneumonia inpatients with parkinsonism and severe dysphagia, of whom seven regained oral intake. No foods or diagnosis-specific results. The same group's 136-person journal study covers earlier 2015–2017 admissions and is a separate cohort.

S-10-10 Tomita reviewed 91 deceased patients meeting UK Brain Bank Parkinson criteria. After oral intake stopped, median survival was 27.6 months in gastrostomy, 6.3 nasogastric and 0.8 parenteral groups. Thirteen ate orally until death. Nonrandomized routes, no food or formula tested.

S-18-4 Shiraishi describes gastrostomy in 28 people with progressive neurologic disease among 134 procedures. Two of ten with Parkinson disease retained concurrent oral intake. No individual foods or preparation-related outcomes.
